post.caption: The Mask of Agamemnon is older than the king it names. In August 1876, Heinrich Schliemann began digging at Mycenae in Greece, where a ring of slabs enclosed five shaft graves. The famous gold mask came from Grave V. Craftsmen hammered a sheet of gold against a wooden form. Schliemann believed he had found Agamemnon's tomb, so the mask took the name Mask of Agamemnon. It dates to around the 16th century BC, about 300 years older than the traditional Trojan War, and it is kept in the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.
